criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs triggers `introspect_job` (a rejected or failed job) while the kill switch is on. It asserts that the fake driver was not invoked, no introspection record was committed with status failed, and one event is pending. Evidence: `cargo test` shows it passing.
criteria.evidence: The test `an_introspection_triggered_while_the_kill_switch_is_on_is_left_pending` passed. It calls `athena.stop()`, then `introspect_job` twice. It asserts that `model.prompts` is empty, the reply was not used, `introspections(&fx)` is empty (so no failed record), exactly one event is pending with the Rejection trigger, and a 'deferred' line was printed. Athena's run of the test with the fix reverted failed (exit 101), but only because the new accessors did not compile.

criteria.criterion: The same test, or a second one, turns the switch off through the real `start` path (`Athena::start` or the `athena start` command). It asserts that the pending event now yields exactly one committed introspection record with status recorded, and that the queue is then empty. Evidence: `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. `start_with` returns true; there is exactly one Recorded introspection for the job, with trigger Rejection; the model was called once; the queue is empty. A second `athena.start()` and the `athena start` binary ('already off') add no record and no model call.

criteria.criterion: A test covers an intervention-triggered introspection while the switch is on. It is deferred and then run on start, and a second `athena start` does not run it again. Evidence: `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. While the switch is on, the intervention gets no record, one event is pending and the model gets no prompt. After `start_with` there is one Recorded introspection with trigger Intervention and the queue is empty. A second `start()` returns false, the record count is still 1 and the model has still been called once.

criteria.criterion: The diff to crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs (and the `start` path in crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs or crates/athena-cli/src/commands.rs) shows the stopped check happening before `driver.invoke`, with a queue of pending events and a drain run when the switch is turned off.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: `run_or_defer` checks `self.state.registry().stopped()` before calling `introspect`, which reaches `driver.invoke` at introspect.rs:1600. The queue is made of `StateDir::introspect_pending_dir`, `defer`, `pending_files` and `pending_introspections`. `start_with` in manage.rs calls `run_pending_introspections` after `registry().start()`. `commands::start` calls `start_with(&Terminal)`. Grep shows the only other callers of `introspect_job` and `introspect_intervention` (run/mod.rs:421, manage.rs:400, reading.rs:1374) all go through `run_or_defer`.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry saying that introspections are deferred while the kill switch is on and run after `athena start`.
criteria.evidence: There is one new bullet under Unreleased/Added: 'Introspections are deferred while the kill switch is on and run after `athena start`...'. It also covers the rerun of the old failures and says no record schema changed.

criteria.criterion: No unrelated behavior changes. The existing tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs and the other crates pass unchanged, and `the_kill_switch_blocks_new_work` still passes. Evidence: `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: I ran `the_kill_switch_blocks_new_work` and it passed. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed (CI run 43390183538). The diff to introspection.rs only adds lines; no existing test body changed. `Athena::start()` keeps its signature. Grep shows the CLI is the only non-test caller of `start`/`start_with`.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` (with -D warnings as configured) and `cargo test` pass, as recorded by Athena on the final tree.

findings.summary: Old kill-switch failures are found by matching a substring of the failure text, and that text is a copy of the driver's error message rather than taken from it.
findings.evidence: `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT = "the kill switch is on"` repeats the `#[error]` text of `DriverError::Stopped` (athena-agent/src/lib.rs:131). If someone rewords that message, the rerun rule silently stops matching. Deriving the text from `DriverError::Stopped.to_string()` would keep the two in step. Free-text matching is acceptable here only because it reads old records, and new deferrals no longer produce these failures.

findings.summary: On the first start, the rerun rule will rerun four introspections, not only the two named jobs.
findings.evidence: The evidence snapshot has four failed introspections with this text: p86y (5c0p), 934p (7mjc), t425 (20261030-065944-4gny) and 2gh7 (20261031-043018-kjy2). The last two jobs failed because 'the producer could not run: the kill switch is on', so their reruns will cost model calls to diagnose a kill-switch stop. The changelog and D177 both say the rule covers more than the two jobs, so this is a known cost.

findings.summary: The tests only fail at compile time without the fix, and rerunning an old failure is tested only for job events.
findings.evidence: Athena's fails-without runs for criteria 1-3 all exited 101 because the code did not compile (no `start_with` or `pending_introspections`), not because an assertion failed. The test asserts the behavior directly, so it would catch a regression once it compiles. The requeue test covers job (Rejection) events only; the branch that requeues intervention events has no test.

summary: The change does what was asked. While the kill switch is on, `introspect_job` and `introspect_intervention` now go through a new `run_or_defer` function. It reads `registry().stopped()` before the model can be called and, if the switch is on, saves the event as a file in `<state>/introspect-pending/` instead of committing a failed record. `athena start` (through the new `Athena::start_with`) runs those saved events and deletes each file once its record is committed. It also queues any event whose only introspections failed with "the kill switch is on", which covers the failed introspections of jobs 20261029-142858-5c0p and 20261017-155259-7mjc. I read both in the evidence snapshot: each has a failed or rejected outcome, so `event_of_job` will rebuild their events. I ran the four new tests and `the_kill_switch_blocks_new_work`, and all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. Every changed file is on the deliverables list, and nothing under records/ or athena.toml changed. D177 is added at the end of docs/decisions.md with a Provenance bullet. There are no blockers or major findings. The minor ones: the rerun rule finds old failures by matching a copied string, and it will also rerun two more jobs that failed because of the kill switch. The changelog and D177 both say the rule can cover more than the two named jobs.
